findings.title: Materials' 65-point lens gap signals peak-cycle earnings
findings.body: Materials shows a 65-point percentile gap between its trailing and forward lenses, the widest in the table, with a trailing P/E of 33.91 at the 81st percentile. Analysts are underwriting 113 percent earnings growth, which would compress the multiple by 53 percent — a bet that current earnings are near a cyclical top, not a new plateau.

findings.title: Consumer Staples' week-long percentile surge defies its cheapness
findings.body: Consumer Staples jumped 25 percentile points in forward valuation in a single week, yet still sits at just the 31st percentile, with a forward P/E of 19.61. The move is concentrated in analyst revisions, not reported earnings, which remain at the 70th percentile — a divergence that suggests the market is repricing the sector's growth outlook faster than its actual results.

findings.title: Real Estate's forward percentile collapse outruns its multiple
findings.body: Real Estate's forward percentile fell 25 points in a month to the 6th percentile, yet its forward P/E of 33.60 remains the highest in the table. The percentile drop reflects a sharp repricing of expected earnings, now projected to decline 3 percent, but the multiple itself has barely moved — leaving a valuation that still assumes the old growth trajectory.
